developing a general AAR system for body-wide anatomy recognition.
the development of a general AAR system that can be easily adapted for a wide range of applications.
the adaptation of an AAR system to a new application, in this case, the quantification, through MRI, of obesity in children with Obstructive Sleep apnea Syndrome (OSA).

our AAR system is capable of recognizing the adipose regions in the abdominal region of obese children with an accuracy of about 3-4 voxels and that the subsequent GC and IRFC algorithms can then be used to delineate them with a low FPVF and a high TPVF.

the adaptation of our AAR system to the new application of quantifying obesity in children via MRI was quite successful, and that it can be easily applied to other similar applications with minimal effort.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the AAR system can be easily and rapidly adapted to a new image modality, new application, and new study subjects, and can provide an initial segmentation of the objects of interest that can then be used as a starting point for more accurate segmentation by model-based GC and IRFC algorithms.
